description: A 16 by 8 grid of keys that a white whale, earthsea, meadowphysics, ansible or teletype connects to as its control surface

params.text: One key of the grid; its brightness is set by the module the grid is connected to, and pressing it sends that key's position to that module

notes: this module has no jacks and produces no voltage. Place it in the patch, then right-click a white whale, earthsea, meadowphysics, ansible or teletype and pick this grid from its menu.
connecting this grid to a second module unplugs it from the first. Clicking the USB jack on a module reclaims the grid for that module.
control-click a key to hold it down while the control key stays down, so several keys can be held at once; on a Mac use command-click. Releasing the control key releases them all.
control-shift-click a key to lock it down until you click it again; on a Mac use command-shift-click. A locked key carries a dot in its lower left corner.
Rack has no multi-touch, so gestures the hardware performs with two hands are done here by holding or locking keys with the modifier keys.
menu: Save grid screenshot — writes a picture of the grid to disk
Mirror hardware grid — mirrors a connected hardware grid onto this one, with a Stop mirroring item to end it
Theme: Red, Orange, Yellow, White — sets the colour and brightness curve of the keys, loosely following the eras of grid hardware
Protocol: 40h, Series, Mext (varibright) — sets which generation of grid this one emulates; Mext is the one to leave it on, the other two match older hardware without variable brightness
Release Locked Keys — releases every key that has been locked down, which pressing Escape with the mouse over the grid also does
